question: Which animal is known as the natural reservoir host for the Ebola virus?
explanation: Spot on! Fruit bats carry the virus naturally without getting sick themselves. Think of them as the original home of the virus in nature.

question: Why do we call Ebola a zoonotic disease?

options.A: It spreads exclusively among wild animals in the forest
options.B: It can only be transmitted through contaminated water
options.C: It mutates rapidly inside human respiratory tracts
options.D: It originates in animals and spreads to humans

explanation: You got it! 'Zoonotic' simply means an infection that jumps from animals to humans. Easy peasy!

question: When the Ebola virus enters the human body, which immune cells does it attack first?
explanation: Spot on! The virus tricks our body by attacking our own defense cells (macrophages and monocytes) right from the start.

question: A community health nurse is teaching villagers how Ebola spreads. Which practice should she warn against the most?

options.A: Drinking boiled water from a community well during dry seasons
options.B: Eating well-cooked pork from certified local livestock farms
options.C: Washing the body of a relative who died from suspected Ebola
options.D: Sharing eating utensils with a family member who has malaria

explanation: Well done! The viral load is super high in someone who just passed away, making traditional burial touching very risky.

question: What is the usual incubation period range for Ebola?
explanation: Correct! Symptoms can show up anywhere from 2 days to 3 weeks after contact. That's why monitoring takes up to 21 days.

question: Which signs and symptoms usually show up first when a person is coming down with Ebola?

options.A: Sudden fever, fatigue, and severe muscle aches
options.B: Profuse internal bleeding and skin bruising
options.C: Paralysis of the lower limbs and blindness
options.D: Productive cough and severe chest congestion

explanation: You nailed it! Early Ebola can easily feel like malaria or typhoid at first—sudden fever and body weakness are the major clues.

question: Why is it so important to quickly isolate a suspected Ebola patient in a clinic?

options.A: It allows the lab to make local drugs
options.B: It prevents the virus from spreading to other patients and healthcare staff
options.C: It eliminates the need to wear protective gowns
options.D: It cures the patient before bleeding starts

explanation: Spot on! Isolating patients cuts off the transmission chain immediately and keeps everyone else in the ward safe.

question: What is the gold-standard laboratory test used to confirm an Ebola infection?

options.A: Routine microscopic examination of red blood cells

explanation: Correct! RT-PCR is the reliable test that catches the virus's RNA in blood samples.

question: What is the main focus of nursing care for a patient with Ebola?

options.B: Placing the patient on complete bed rest without food or water
options.C: Providing supportive care like fluid replacement and symptom relief

explanation: You got it! Since it's a virus, nursing care is all about keeping the patient hydrated and comfortable while their immune system fights.

question: An Ebola patient is vomiting and having terrible watery diarrhea. What is the nurse's priority action?

options.A: Stop all oral meds until diarrhea clears up
options.B: Start aggressive rehydration therapy to correct fluid and electrolyte losses
options.C: Restrict all oral fluids to give the tummy a rest
options.D: Apply warm compresses to stop belly cramps

explanation: Spot on! Replacing lost fluids quickly is lifesaving because dehydration and shock are the big dangers here.

question: Which part of wearing Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) is most risky for accidentally contaminating yourself?
explanation: Correct! Taking off dirty gear takes the most care because you might accidentally touch germs on the outside. Always follow the steps carefully!

question: Which of these is a BIG NO-ROUTINE in infection control during an Ebola outbreak?

options.A: Decontaminating room surfaces with chlorine solutions
options.B: Reusing disposable gloves after washing them with ordinary soap
options.C: Limiting the number of staff entering the isolation zone
options.D: Using a trained buddy to watch you remove your PPE

explanation: You got it! Disposable gloves are strictly one-time-use. Never wash and reuse them—safety first!

question: How long must close contacts of an Ebola patient be watched for signs of illness?
explanation: Spot on! Since the incubation period is up to 21 days, we keep track of contacts for that full period to catch any early signs.

question: Why is building trust with the community so vital during an Ebola outbreak?

options.A: It stops the virus from becoming airborne
options.B: It lets the government cancel travel bans
options.C: It prevents families from hiding sick relatives and encourages early reporting
options.D: It gives clinic staff higher pay

explanation: Correct! When people trust health workers, they bring sick family members in early instead of hiding them, which stops the spread.

question: What do we mean by Post-Ebola Syndrome?

options.A: A collection of chronic physical symptoms persisting after recovery
options.B: A permanent mental illness from the incubation period
options.C: An acute respiratory infection before fever starts
options.D: A sudden relapse of active internal bleeding on day two

explanation: You got it! Even after beating the virus, survivors can deal with lingering joint pain, fatigue, and vision issues.

question: What crucial advice must a nurse give to a male patient who has just recovered from Ebola?

options.A: Return to the isolation ward immediately for another vaccine
options.B: Use barrier contraception or practice safe sex because the virus can linger in semen
options.C: Take daily antibiotics to clear the virus from your joints
options.D: Avoid all physical contact with family forever

explanation: Spot on! The virus can hide in certain body fluids long after recovery, so safe sex guidance is a must for male survivors.
